# The four built-in nodes (window, timer, slot, errorBoundary) dispatch on the
# #[builtin] mark of whatever the target resolves to. That resolution has to
# follow a qualified target too: under `import s "sngl://std"` the node is
# written `s.slot`, and resolving it by bare name silently produced an ordinary
# empty component that dropped its children.

sngl check slot.sngl
stdout 'slot.sngl: ok'
sngl generate --out slotout slot.sngl
grep 'inner' slotout/index.html

sngl check window.sngl
stdout 'window.sngl: ok'
sngl generate --out winout window.sngl
grep 'Hello' winout/index.html

sngl check timer.sngl
stdout 'timer.sngl: ok'

sngl check boundary.sngl
stdout 'boundary.sngl: ok'

# Dispatch follows the resolved declaration, not the spelling: another
# package's ordinary `slot` component reached through its own alias is a plain
# component, not the built-in node.
sngl generate --out shadowout shadowed.sngl
grep 'from widgets' shadowout/index.html

-- slot.sngl --
import s "sngl://std"

component Card() list<component> {
    s.vbox {
        s.slot
    }
}

component main {
    s.window #w(href="/index.html") {
        Card {
            s.text(value="inner")
        }
    }
}

output { none { html } }
-- window.sngl --
import s "sngl://std"

component main {
    s.window #home(href="/index.html") {
        s.text(value="Hello")
    }
}

output { none { html } }
-- timer.sngl --
import s "sngl://std"

component main {
    var n int = 0
    s.timer(interval=1s) {
        n = n + 1
    }
    s.text(value="tick")
}
-- boundary.sngl --
import s "sngl://std"

component main {
    s.errorBoundary(@error(e) {}) {
        s.text(value="body")
    }
}
-- widgets/lib.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

component slot() {
    text(value="from widgets")
}
-- shadowed.sngl --
import s "sngl://std"
import w "widgets"

component main {
    s.window #w2(href="/index.html") {
        w.slot
    }
}

output { none { html } }
